title: fix(payments): never return or keep client Stripe PaymentSheet credentials (B-SECRETS-3)
body:
> **Status (2026-10-05, fix round 9).** Fix round 9 is pushed at `e0cc97e150384d049823327b274ac47511ee952e` (one commit on `bc399edd`). History since round 7: fix round 8 (OP-SIZE-118, test move only, `f80f0088`) moved `test/checkout-hosted-activation-once.spec.ts` to #702 (dual APPROVE at `f80f0088`); B-661R-119 then refreshed the branch: `010f9b57` merged recurring `8c925944` (conflicts resolved in `checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts` and `checkout.service.ts`) and `bc399edd` merged main `ee55f814` cleanly (operator RESTACK NOTE 5998643247). Round 9 closes Sol B-661-14 and Opus B-661-15 (one defect): the native first grant now erases the spent PaymentSheet credentials in its locked write; it also adds the C-661-2 operator backfill script. Size 2,942 / 3,000. Regression and backfill tests are in the tests-only PR #702 (stacked on this branch), which lands with this PR. Fix-round table: PR comment "FIX ROUND 9 (B-661R2-120, agent 120)". Needs both lenses at the exact heads. Do not merge without audit.

**Tier:** T4.
**Why:** Money-path credential handling: the client's Stripe PaymentIntent `client_secret` and customer ephemeral key were returned by owner/admin routes and kept at rest after the payment ended.
**T4 trigger scan:** payments/Stripe data path: YES (webhook transitions now erase cached credentials; checkout replay answer changes for finished payments). Fix round 2: `payment_intent.succeeded` (and its charge-id prefetch) also claims a `payment_failed` row of the same PaymentIntent (entitlement + split on a retried success): YES; the replay classifier runs before every cached-credential return, including the race-loser poll: YES. Auth/tenancy: no change (route guards untouched; only response shape). Schema/migration: NO. New env name: NO. Workflow, `scripts/ci/*`, branch protection: NO. Logging/redaction: YES (stricter only). Fix round 3 (B-661-3): `payment_intent.payment_failed` only writes a purchase that may still fail (compare-and-set on `pending` / `payment_failed`); it never rewrites `canceled` / `expired` / `refunded` / `disputed` / `chargeback_lost`; a settled purchase (`paid`, `active`, ...) loses access only when Stripe's current PaymentIntent status is `requires_payment_method` / `canceled` (read out of the webhook tx in `prefetchForOuterTx`, never Stripe HTTP inside it); an unknown status or a lost compare-and-set throws 503 so the webhook tx rolls back and Stripe redelivers; the metadata fallback only adopts a pending purchase with no PaymentIntent: YES (money, entitlement). Fix round 4: `payment_intent.succeeded` (and its charge-id prefetch) activates a `payment_failed` purchase only when it is the PaymentSheet purchase of that PaymentIntent (`stripe_checkout_session_id` = PaymentIntent id); a hosted Checkout purchase activates only through `checkout.session.completed`, which no longer re-activates `paid` / `canceled` / `expired` / `refunded` / `disputed` / `chargeback_lost` purchases (read fence plus a status condition on the activation write); a prefetched PaymentIntent status applies only to the purchase version (id, status, `updated_at`) read before the Stripe call, and the revoke is a compare-and-set on that version; a success that activates nothing still moves `updated_at` on the entitled purchases of that PaymentIntent; Stripe 4xx other than 429 on the status lookup is a logged no-op: YES (money, entitlement). Fix round 5: `payment_intent.succeeded` locks the PaymentIntent's purchases and writes compare-and-set (a terminal state committed first wins, 503 + redelivery otherwise); a one-time purchase activated before and then failed is re-entitled by its PaymentIntent's success and its payment-failure-canceled drops are pending again; a settled purchase's decline revokes only on the same `xmin` row version under `FOR UPDATE`; Stripe 401 / 403 on the status lookup now retry: YES (money, entitlement). Schema/migration: still NO (`xmin` is a PostgreSQL system column). Fix round 6: `payment_intent.succeeded` recovers the activated, payment-failed one-time purchases of its PaymentIntent (looked up by activation record) before it looks for a purchase to activate, so a never-activated purchase that a decline adopted onto the same PaymentIntent never hides them; every drop cancel other than the payment failure itself (refund, dispute, cancel, coach "Unassign drops", grant revoke) also takes over the drops that failure canceled, so a recovery never restores drops a coach unassigned after the failure; the purchase row locks are `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (still block every UPDATE / DELETE of the row, no longer block inserts that reference it): YES (money, entitlement, drops). Workflow: YES, test-only (`mwb-3-live-tests` runs one more live spec). Schema/migration: NO. Fix round 9: `invoice.paid` and `customer.subscription.updated` erase `stripe_client_secret` / `stripe_ephemeral_key` in the same locked update that grants a native subscription access (first invoice paid, or the trial's own card saved); an attempt that grants nothing keeps them: YES (credentials, money path). New operator script `scripts/clear-spent-payment-credentials.ts` (writes production data only when the operator runs it with `--apply`): YES (data). Schema/migration: NO. Workflow: NO. Fix round 7: the recovery lookup (`activatedFailedPurchases`) filters `payment_failed`, an activation record (`fanout: { isNot: null }`), one-time billing and no subscription in the query, then limits to ten, so other rows of the PaymentIntent can never fill the limit: YES (money, entitlement). Schema/migration: NO. Workflow: NO.
**T3 trigger scan:** Admin API response shape: the two credential fields disappear from `GET /v1/admin/payments/purchases`, `GET /v1/admin/payments/purchases/:id` and the admin dunning view/actions. All other columns, including every Stripe id, stay. New 409 codes on `POST` payment-intent replay of a finished key: `PAYMENT_ALREADY_COMPLETE`, `PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_CLOSED`, and (fix round 2, C-661-4) `PAYMENT_REFUNDED_OR_IN_REVIEW` for refunded / disputed / chargeback_lost rows.
**Bounded T1:** none.
**Builder-owner:** agent 113 (B-FEE-R7 lane, follow-up B-SECRETS-3); fix round 2: agent 115 (B-FEE-9); fix round 3: agent 116 (B-661-116); fix round 4: agent 116 (B-661-R4-116); fix round 5: agent 117 (B-661-R5-117); fix round 6: agent 117 (B-661-R6-117); fix round 7: agent 117 (B-661-R7-117); fix round 8: operator agent 118 (OP-SIZE-118); main refresh: agent 119 (B-661R-119); fix round 9: agent 120 (B-661R2-120).
**Acceptance evidence:** Fix round 9: tests in #702: `test/checkout-grant-credentials.spec.ts` (real handler on the recurring fakes) and a new block in `test/checkout-settlement.live.spec.ts` (`mwb-3-live-tests`, real PostgreSQL: the AUD-SOL-661D-120 acceptance cases, unsaved-trial controls, and the backfill over 13 spent / 6 payable / 1 credential-free rows). Failing-before (src = `bc399edd` + the script, handler fix absent): 9 failed / 20 passed, only the credential assertions, `tsc --noEmit` green, [run 37348121187](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37348121187). After, with both lenses' probes replayed: 44 suites / 609 tests, `tsc --noEmit` green, [run 37348700674](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37348700674). Fix round 7: tests in #702 (tests-only, stacked on this branch; `test/checkout-settlement.live.spec.ts` in `mwb-3-live-tests`): the activated owner behind 9 / 10 / 12 never-activated purchases adopted onto its PaymentIntent (real `CheckoutService` reservations with provider replies held, real decline adoptions in concurrent held transactions, unordered reads answered newest first) recovers (`payment_recovered`, paid, entitled, drop pending), the adopted purchases gain nothing, nothing runs twice, and a redelivery is a no-op. Failing-before (the #702 tests against `c7ee15f0`): 2 failed / 31 passed in [run 37186266591](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37186266591) (10 and 12 fail, 9 is the control). After (this head plus #702): 190 / 190, `tsc --noEmit` green, in [run 37186426457](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37186426457). In this PR only the round-5 double learns the PurchaseFanout relation filter. Fix round 6: `test/checkout-settlement.live.spec.ts` (new, runs in `mwb-3-live-tests` on real PostgreSQL with the full schema: the real handler, `PurchaseFanoutService`, `PartialRefundDecisionService` and Prisma). C-661-12 (the Opus round-5 probe): `xmin` changes on a write with an equal `updated_at`, not on a lock or a rolled-back write; a decline witnessed before a success is retried (503), a fresh one revokes and cancels the drop; a late completion is `already_progressed`; the success recovers once and its redelivery is a no-op; a refund holding the row wins over a success waiting on the PaymentIntent lock; a missed compare-and-set is P2025; two concurrent successes activate once. B-661-3: an activated failed owner and a never-activated adopted purchase on one PaymentIntent, in both insertion orders: the owner recovers (paid, entitled, drop pending), the adopted purchase stays `payment_failed`, unentitled, without an activation record. B-661-9: a coach "Unassign drops" committed after the failure keeps the drop canceled through the recovery ("Keep drops" control restores it); the decision racing the recovery in both commit orders leaves the drop canceled, and the second transaction waits on the first's row lock. C-661-11: while a transaction holds both purchase locks, another connection inserts a row that references the purchase without waiting, and an UPDATE of the purchase still waits. Failing-before (tests only, src = `957e3677` + main): 7 failed / 154 passed in [run 37183409605](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183409605) (B-661-3 adopted-first, B-661-9 Unassign + both races, C-661-11 real-PostgreSQL and two SQL-text assertions; the controls pass). After: 161 / 161 in [run 37183417176](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183417176). Lane-only global setup starts the runner's PostgreSQL; it is not in this PR. Fix round 5: `test/checkout-settlement-round5.spec.ts` (new; real handler and real `PurchaseFanoutService` on a double whose every write bumps a row version like PostgreSQL xmin): the Sol sequence with the success written in the same millisecond as the witnessed version (retried, never applied; the redelivery is `stale_failure`) plus a next-millisecond control; the settled decline checks the row version under `FOR UPDATE`; an activated hosted purchase whose payment really failed is recovered by the same PaymentIntent's success (paid, entitled, drops canceled by that failure pending again, a refund-canceled drop stays canceled, no second fanout / first-payment notice / split; redelivery no-op); a late completion after that failure is `already_progressed`; B-661-8 for `refunded` / `canceled` / `expired` / `disputed` / `chargeback_lost` committed between the success's read and write (503, no resurrection, redelivery leaves it), a pending PaymentSheet case, a two-delivery race (one activation), and the PaymentIntent row lock taken before the read; C-661-8 401 / 403 retried, 404 / 400 dropped with an error-level log; C-661-9 completion write fence (passes before by design); controls: never-activated adopted hosted purchase, PaymentSheet decline then retry, refund before the read. Failing-before (tests only, src = `6fdc35de` + main): 17 failed / 59 passed in [run 37179739922](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37179739922). Sol's round-4 probe, adapted only to supply a row version and the activation record: 12 / 12 at the fix. Fix round 4: `test/checkout-hosted-activation-once.spec.ts` (new; the Opus probe harness with its assertions inverted: one hosted session declined then retried activates once, by completion, with its access window, hosted fanout and one deferred split; redeliveries and a duplicate completion change nothing; two open sessions: session B is never entitled by session A's charge; PaymentSheet control; C-661-7 for six statuses) and the round-4 cases in the `B-661-3` block of `test/checkout-webhook-handler.spec.ts` (the Sol sequence on a PaymentSheet purchase; a hosted provisional purchase whose PaymentIntent success commits after the stale read; the no-tx race; C-661-6 404 no-op with a 429 control). Failing-before (tests only, src = `a193d7e1` + main): 13 failed / 51 passed in [run 37175121818](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37175121818). Fix round 3: the `B-661-3 a late-delivered earlier decline never revokes a successful retry` block in `test/checkout-webhook-handler.spec.ts` (failed -> succeeded -> late earlier decline, in-tx and no-tx; unknown Stripe status throws with no in-tx Stripe call; success committing between the decline's read and write; final statuses never rewritten; metadata fallback never adopts a purchase that holds another PaymentIntent; prefetch only when settled; controls: ordinary decline, real failure after settlement) and `B-661-3: does NOT cancel drops ...` in `test/cancel-pending-on-refund.spec.ts`. Failing-before (tests only, src = `f4679fd8`): 13 failed / 50 passed in [run 37171991379](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171991379). Fix round 2: the `B-661-1` / `B-661-2` / `C-661-4` tests in `test/checkout.service.spec.ts` (7 finished statuses with credentials still at rest, failed-payment resume control, P2002 + webhook-settlement interleavings) and the `B-661-1 decline, then a successful retry` block in `test/checkout-webhook-handler.spec.ts`; failing-before on a tests-only branch (see the fix-round comment). Round 1: `test/b-secrets-3-admin-credentials.spec.ts` (new), B-SECRETS-3 cases in `test/checkout-webhook-handler.spec.ts` and `test/checkout.service.spec.ts`. Failing-before: 10 of 11 new tests fail on `origin/main` sources (the 11th is the structural omit-constant control). After: 9 suites, 258 tests pass locally (`jest --runInBand` on the touched suites); ESLint clean on changed files. tsc and full suites run in CI.
**Promotion triggers:** re-audit if any route starts returning a ClientPurchase row without `ADMIN_PURCHASE_OMIT` / a coach allow-list, or if a new terminal ClientPurchase transition is added without `CLEARED_PAYMENT_SECRETS`. C-661-3: #654 (now split; its webhooks are in #680) edits the same `applySubscriptionDeleted` data block and stores a first-invoice / SetupIntent secret; whichever of #661 / the #678-#680 stack merges second keeps `...CLEARED_PAYMENT_SECRETS` in both branches of `applySubscriptionDeleted` and on the stack's activation path (invoice.paid -> active / trialing). Fix round 9 (#661 lands second) carries the activation half in both grant writes. B-661-3 composition: #680 adds a recurring-subscription early return in `applyPaymentIntentFailed` right after the metadata fallback; whichever merges second keeps that early return before the B-661-3 status fence. Re-audit if any new ClientPurchase status is added without placing it in one of the three decline classes (claimable, final, settled). Round 4 composition (C-661-3): whichever of #661 / the #678-#680 stack merges second applies `activatesOnPaymentIntentSuccess` (PaymentSheet-only claim of a `payment_failed` purchase) to any recurring PaymentSheet / first-invoice purchase the stack adds, and keeps the C-661-7 completion fence for one-time purchases. Round 5 composition (C-661-3): the decline's version is PostgreSQL `xmin`, so raw-SQL writes are covered without `updated_at`; whichever of #661 / the #678-#680 stack merges second routes any new `payment_intent.succeeded` write through the same PaymentIntent row lock and compare-and-set (`writeIfUnchanged`), and keeps the recovery branch one-time only (`billing_type` not recurring, no subscription). Re-audit if a PurchaseFanout row can be deleted while its purchase exists: recovery uses it as the activation record. Round 6: every drop cancel goes through `cancelPendingForPurchase` (a new cancel path written directly on ScheduledDrop must also take over `canceled:payment_failed` drops); a new coach-relationship end that keeps a purchase in `payment_failed` must cancel its drops through it too. A `payment_intent.succeeded` change must keep the recovery lookup ahead of the activation lookup. Round 7: the recovery lookup must keep its activation / one-time / subscription conditions inside the query, before any limit.

## What changed

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-646-1 (Opus): admin purchase list and drill-down return the raw row with `stripe_client_secret` / `stripe_ephemeral_key` | `src/checkout/admin-purchase.select.ts`: `ADMIN_PURCHASE_OMIT` (Prisma `omit`, every other column stays). Applied to `listPurchases` and `getPurchase`. | 91625c86 | "GET /v1/admin/payments/purchases", "GET /v1/admin/payments/purchases/:id" |
| C-646-1 (Sol): `DunningService.getAdminView` returns the raw purchase (admin dunning view plus advance/reset/cancel responses) | Same omit; `DunningAdminView.purchase` is typed `AdminPurchaseView`. | 91625c86 | "DunningService.getAdminView ..." |
| C-646-2 (Opus): cached credentials are never cleared | `CLEARED_PAYMENT_SECRETS` is written by `payment_intent.succeeded`, `checkout.session.expired` and `customer.subscription.deleted`. `payment_intent.payment_failed` keeps them (the client retries the same PaymentIntent). A replay of a finished key no longer waits 5 s for a secret that never comes and then answers `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`; it answers 409 `PAYMENT_ALREADY_COMPLETE` ("This payment is already complete. Your package is ready in your account.") or `PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_CLOSED` ("This checkout has closed. Start again from the package page to buy it."). No new Stripe call. | 91625c86 | "payment_intent.succeeded erases ...", "checkout.session.expired erases them too", "a replay after the payment is paid / expired ..." |
| C-646-2 (Sol): log redaction | `REDACT_KEYS` gains `stripe_client_secret`, `stripe_ephemeral_key`, `ephemeral_key`; any `*_secret` / `*ephemeral_key` key is redacted; Stripe credential values (`pi_/seti_..._secret_...`, `ek_`, `sk_`/`rk_` live/test, `whsec_`) are scrubbed from free text in both `redactObject` and `redactLogLine`. Ids such as `pi_...` stay readable. | 91625c86 | three "log redaction" canary tests |
| ADMIN_PURCHASE_OMIT guard | Asserts the omit drops exactly the credential columns and that no other credential-like ClientPurchase column exists. | 91625c86 | "ADMIN_PURCHASE_OMIT drops exactly the credential columns" |

## Not in this PR

- **C-627-8 (Opus, stale repay amount in the failed-transfer log):** closed in #627 itself (fix round 9, `6910d747`): the alert now names `owed_cents_at_failure` and the live reconciliation gap to re-read before repaying.
- Existing rows (C-661-2, operator decision): since fix round 2 the replay API never returns cached credentials of a finished payment (status is classified first). Fix round 9 adds the backfill as `scripts/clear-spent-payment-credentials.ts` (dry run by default; `--apply` erases in bounded batches; idempotent; counts only in its output). It covers one-time and subscription rows and keeps every still-payable attempt: a one-time attempt in `pending` / `payment_failed`, and a subscription attempt in `pending` / `incomplete` / `payment_failed` / `trialing` that is not entitled and never started a trial. The old one-status predicate is not used (it would erase a payable trial's SetupIntent). Running it in production is an operator decision for the deploy window; this PR runs nothing.
- `payment_intent.canceled` is not a subscribed checkout webhook event today; a canceled PaymentIntent leaves its row pending. Adding it needs the Stripe endpoint event list changed (operator).
- Round 4, pre-existing and outside this diff: the PaymentSheet activation path (`payment_intent.succeeded`) never sets `access_expires_at` (same on main); a duplicate `checkout.session.completed` of a recurring purchase that is already `active` is not fenced (subscription events may set `active` before completion, and completion must still run fanout and split); `ClientPurchase.stripe_payment_intent_id` has no index (every PaymentIntent event scans; candidate for a later migration).
- C-661-10 (Opus, pre-existing, follow-up): the metadata fallback can stamp one session's PaymentIntent on another session's row, so lookups by `stripe_payment_intent_id` can match two rows. Round 5 locks every row of the PaymentIntent and fences each write on its own state; releasing the PaymentIntent on completion and an index on `stripe_payment_intent_id` stay a follow-up (the index is a migration). Round 6 recovery finds the activated owner of the PaymentIntent before any other row (B-661-3); round 7 selects it in the query itself, so no number of other rows of the PaymentIntent hides it.
- Mobile should map the two new 409 codes; until then the app shows its standard fallback with the request reference.

(7 statuses), "(control) a failed payment that holds its credentials resumes", "a failed payment whose credentials are gone" |

| B-661-3 (Sol): a late-delivered earlier decline flips a paid, successfully retried purchase to `payment_failed` and drops access | `applyPaymentIntentFailed`: `pending` / `payment_failed` -> compare-and-set `updateMany` on that status (a success that commits first wins); `canceled` / `expired` / `refunded` / `disputed` / `chargeback_lost` -> never rewritten; any other (settled) status -> Stripe's current PaymentIntent status decides: `requires_payment_method` / `canceled` ends access (real failure, drops canceled), anything else is a no-op (`stale_failure`). The status is read in `prefetchForOuterTx` (out of the tx, only for settled purchases); missing inside the tx or a lost compare-and-set -> 503 `PAYMENT_FAILURE_RETRY`, tx rolls back, Stripe redelivers. Logs carry ids and error codes only. | 57fa2402 | `B-661-3 a late-delivered earlier decline never revokes a successful retry` (12 red before, 3 controls pass both ways), `B-661-3: does NOT cancel drops ...` (red before); failing-before run 37171991379 |

## Fix round 4

Full table: PR comment "FIX ROUND 4 (B-661-R4-116, agent 116)". Merged origin/main `f57baba3` (merge `d2399d2e`) and `a5b605d1` (merge `6fdc35de`); both automatic, main touched no file of this PR.

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-661-3 (Sol): a PaymentIntent status prefetched before the tx revokes access after a failure and a successful same-PaymentIntent retry committed in between | `prefetchForOuterTx` reads the purchase version (id, status, `updated_at`) before asking Stripe and returns it as `paymentIntentWitnessById`. Inside the tx a settled purchase is judged only when it is still that version; otherwise 503 `PAYMENT_FAILURE_RETRY` (`purchase_changed`), the tx rolls back and the redelivery reads Stripe again. The revoke is `updateMany` on id + status + `updated_at`. The no-tx path asks Stripe after reading the purchase. A success that activates nothing moves `updated_at` on the entitled purchases of its PaymentIntent, so a hosted provisional purchase records the settlement too. | 0e079bb8 | round-4 cases in `B-661-3 ...` (`test/checkout-webhook-handler.spec.ts`) |
| B-661-5 (Opus): `payment_intent.succeeded` activates a hosted Checkout purchase that a decline adopted; completion then activates it again | `activatesOnPaymentIntentSuccess`: `pending`, or `payment_failed` only when `stripe_checkout_session_id` equals the PaymentIntent id (PaymentSheet). Same rule in the charge-id prefetch. A hosted purchase gets `claimed: false`, `checkout_session_activates` and activates once through `checkout.session.completed`. | 0e079bb8 | `test/checkout-hosted-activation-once.spec.ts` |
| C-661-6 (Opus): Stripe 4xx on the status lookup answers 503 until Stripe stops retrying | 4xx other than 429 -> `payment_intent_unreadable`: logged with ids and the Stripe code, purchase unchanged, event acknowledged. 429, 5xx and network errors still 503. | 0e079bb8 | `C-661-6: Stripe answers 404 ...`, `(control) C-661-6: a 429 ...` |
| C-661-7 (Opus): a late `checkout.session.completed` re-activates a refunded / canceled / already activated purchase | Read fence: `paid`, `canceled`, `expired`, `refunded`, `disputed`, `chargeback_lost` -> `already_progressed`, no write, no fanout, no split. The activation write also carries `status notIn` that list, so a refund or cancel that commits after the read rolls the event back. | 0e079bb8 | `C-661-7 checkout.session.completed activates only a purchase that was never activated` (6 statuses) and the adopted-decline control |
| C-661-2 (Opus, operator) / C-661-3 (composition) | No code. Backfill stays an operator deploy-window item; composition notes under Promotion triggers. | - | - |

## Fix round 5

Full table: PR comment "FIX ROUND 5 (B-661-R5-117, agent 117)". Merged origin/main `643817b3` with merge commit `a88746a0` (merge-only, automatic; main touched no file of this PR). Tests `8f5f7d9f` before fix `957e3677`.

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-661-3 (Sol): equal `updated_at` lets a stale decline revoke a settled purchase | The purchase version is PostgreSQL `xmin` (`SELECT status, xmin::text ...`), read before the Stripe lookup. In the tx the revoke re-reads it `FOR UPDATE` and writes only on the same version (`updateMany` on id + status); otherwise 503 `purchase_changed`.
